intro_html: Sudado means sweated, and that is exactly what happens here. Pork chops go into a covered pot with tomato, onion, green onion and cilantro, and everything steams down into its own sauce with hardly any liquid added. Potatoes and carrots cook right in it. In Colombia this is Tuesday dinner, served over white rice, and it is one of the most efficient one-pot dishes on the planet.
cost_closing_html: About $2.58 a bowl, and the pork chops are nearly the entire bill. The potatoes, carrots and tomatoes that make up the rest of the pot barely register.
shop_smart: Buy the family pack of bone-in pork chops. Bone-in costs less per pound than boneless and the bones make the sauce taste like it simmered all day.
Potatoes in the big bag are the cheapest calories in the store. This pot uses a lot of them, and buying the ten pound bag instead of loose is one of the biggest single savings in the whole recipe.
Sazon seasoning is the shortcut Colombian cooks actually use. A box of packets costs very little and it delivers the color and savor that would otherwise take a long list of jars.
Green onions and cilantro are the finish, not the base. One bunch of each is plenty. Chop them in at the very end so they stay bright instead of stewing into nothing.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the pork chops with salt, black pepper, ground cumin and the sazon seasoning, then brown them in the vegetable oil in a heavy pot, in batches, until both sides have color.
Cook the diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until soft, scraping up whatever the pork left behind.
Add the diced tomatoes with their juice and let them cook down for about five minutes into a thick base.
Return the pork chops to the pot, tuck in the sliced carrots and the peeled and quartered potatoes, cover tightly, and cook on low heat for about an hour.
Resist adding water. The vegetables and tomato give off enough liquid to make the sauce, and that is where the flavor concentration comes from.
When the potatoes are fork tender, stir in the chopped green onions and cilantro and taste for salt. Cook the rice per the package to serve underneath.
portion_html: Spread the cooked rice across your 14 containers, then set the pot on your scale, subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1, divide by 14, and spoon that exact weight of pork, potatoes and sauce over the rice. Every plate lands near 670 calories with 54 grams of protein, which is one of the highest protein numbers in this batch.

head.description: Pork chops sweated with tomato, potatoes and carrots into their own sauce, served over rice. A 14 serving Colombian sudado de cerdo for meal prep.
head.keywords: sudado de cerdo, colombian pork stew, pork and potato stew, one pot pork recipe, budget meal prep, cheap dinner ideas
steps: Season the pork chops with cumin and sazon and brown them in oil in batches.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot, then add the diced tomatoes and reduce.
Return the pork and add the carrots and potatoes, then cover tightly.
Cook on low about an hour without adding water, until the potatoes are tender.
Finish with green onions and cilantro and serve over cooked rice.
